tips.comment: The yard had a great time at Newmarket, and Bowmark looked a good prospect when winning on the debut. He is out of Kingman, which the Gosdens have had success with previously.

Royal Playwright flopped in his last race of the season in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster when finishing last of 8. However, the last 6 horses were fairly close together, and that included the 3rd, Wimbledon Hawkeye, to whom he finished 2nd in his previous race, the Group 2 Royal Lodge at Newmarket. So, he finished the season running against high-level opposition. Andrew Balding's horses are outperforming this season so far, and Royal Playwright won his first two-year-old race impressively at Salisbury. He could start his three-year-old career likewise with a win.
He has won two in a row, including on the Kempton surface, which plays similar. His bloodlines won a renewal of this race a few years ago.

Irish raider. The 3yo colt was a nice 3L winner on his debut six weeks ago, posting a high RPR rating. A useful-looking A O’Brien runner was in third that day. The runner-up has run well in a Group 3 since. Some unexposed rivals in this Listed contest, and the selection looks the value bet.

Michael Scofield is an American bred 3yo by Belmont Stakes winner and half-brother was a well rated winner at Grade 2 level in the States. Irish trained by Michael O'Callaghan, comes here following two straight-forward victories at Southwell. Interesting to see if he can take this step up to Listed class. Potential.

Has the advantage of being the only C&D winner in this field and also finished a credible 2 of 9 here over C&D last month. Taking into account the fact he is going up 3 classes, I still think he is overpriced.

Up 6 lbs for Trial Day win when overcoming a wide trip to win fairly comfortably. Trainer wasn't sure he'd like Lingfield, but he'd won here at Newcastle the time before, so today's track is not a worry. Only 3 years old, plenty of improvement is possible to come. May defy the rise bearing in mind the Trials win wouldn't have suited. Sired by Too Darn Hot from a Lope De Vega mare, he's bred to progress.

Berkshire Whisper was well backed when winning nicely here last time and has progressed steadily with each start. The form of his debut is stacking up well, and now switched to handicaps, there’s likely more to come. Yard won this last year, is in form, and thrives with handicappers at Newcastle (107 runs, 23 wins, 1.36 A/E, +33pts @ 30% ROI).
Marchogion was behind a couple of these when last out, with both of them taking on weight for that last run. I think this puts my pick in with a shout with the better draw as well.

The 7/1 looks an e/w steal to me for this progressive horse, which already has some cracking form in the book. This colt showed a great attitude to only go down by a head last time out to a horse that's since performed well in a Group 3 race. Prior to that, Hello Zaman had won well at this trip in another AW race when he had the race sewn up and was eased down. It's that 2nd last time out, though, which is the key for me, and the trainer has his string in great order, so the 7/1 looks very generous, I'd suggest.
Narrowly denied LTO at Southwell when giving 10 lbs to the winner, but the win on penultimate start beating Rebels Gamble looks strong form and may have more to offer here.
Dropping back to 6 furlongs will very much be in this one's favor this afternoon. Twice a winner over this distance and with 4 places on offer, it looks very good each way value to me.

Starting at a good each-way price of 12/1, this Willie Haggas-trained runner has had a good season on the all-weather and can carry that on here. Well drawn in 16 and should get to the front and could prove difficult to pass.

Has been beaten by two of today's rivals in their last 2 runs @ Southwell and over C/D @ this class 2 level, but was not beaten that far in either race and connections clearly think they can turn it around here. Is a C/D winner, top jockey up and very shrewd trainer is 22 percent with his 3yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 18/1 solid Ew value in the race.
He wasn't far behind Zaman, who is higher up in the betting last time and has a much better draw for this contest here.

Soldiers Star got the job done well at Kempton last time off 73 and the form’s already been boosted by the runner-up winning since. Drops back to 6f here which shouldn’t be an issue, and with the trainer going well in handicaps at Lingfield (108 runs, 23 wins, 1.16 A/E, +38pts @ 35% ROI), he’s firmly in the mix again.

Cloud Cover took this race last year off a much lower mark but looked to have plenty in hand when winning a fillies’ handicap here last time off 100. She’s had a wind op since, comes in fresh, and with the yard flying and a profitable jockey combo, she’s very much the one to beat again.

Consistent mare this season, and after 3 solid placed efforts, gained first victory for 21 months when running out a comfortable winner over this trip at Lingfield in February. Can find enough improvement to defy a 5 lbs higher mark.
The jockey Rossa Ryan has had a great all-weather season, and Aramis Grey has all the form to bother the favorite in this contest. Recently, 3rd at Lingfield was good form.
He really enjoys his trips to Newcastle and almost won over this course and distance last time. Was on a hat trick not long ago.

The 4yo filly has 4 wins from 8 and twice a runner-up, looking progressive. Front runner who has a high cruising speed. Two wins and a narrow defeat in her three starts this year, and only slightly higher in the weights now. Unexposed over this 7f trip and she has a strong jockey booking. The fav in the race looks smart but he does like to be held up and with 14 runners he could meet some trouble.
Has won on 2 of the last 4 starts and finished a good 2nd on the latest outing at Wolverhampton 13 days ago. Should be there or thereabouts.
Viennoise has steadily improved from race to race this season. At a very tempting price, it must have an each-way chance if performing as well again.

Showed promise on first 2 AW runs, over 1m2f at Lingfield, when beaten 1¾ & 2¾ lengths and I think we could give her the benefit of the doubt in her only run since when dropping to the rear having been short of room over 1f out and finishing 9 lengths behind the winner There are a few question marks regarding this runner as she returns after a 4 months break and having her debut run since changing yards and also having a first run on a Tapeta surface, but, having shown potential in 2 of her last 3 runs and running off a similar mark today, her odds of 15.00 with 4 places on offer are big enough for me to chance an EW bet on this runner whose yard is on a 22% SR in the last 14 days

Race 3 at Newcastle today is the Fillies' And Mares' Championships Handicap (Class 2) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,421 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old filly Gaiety Musical from the Paul David Evans yard, and she will be ridden by Joe Fanning. This daughter of Gregorian is a 4-time winner and is holding her form well enough to warrant a decent showing in this race, especially with her eye-catching win at her last start.

The maiden tag for CALLIANASSA is a concern but the nearest she came to shaking off the tag was in a class two over this trip with claimer Ethan Tindall in the saddle. She's four pounds lighter in the weights here so it's tricky to rule her out if she matches that run. Worth a look as even the each-way return is tasty with the extra places.

She was superb winning here over C&D last month and performed okay here again LTO when 4th of 8 last month. She should welcome the dropped mark but has to overcome going up 3 classes. Still, she is overpriced in my opinion.

Sent off a strong 6/4 favorite last time at Kempton but never really looked comfortable in the race before running on into 3rd. Has plenty of questions to answer here and will need luck in running, but with trainer John Gosden in fantastic form, he has a great chance.

Progressive 4-year-old, Night of Thunder colt. Won last twice out over course and distance. Running for a yard in very good form who go well at the track. Has beaten a lot of these already. Might be less well handicapped but should have more to come.
Hard to see how the bookies have him as low as 12/1 given the dominant performance last time out. Hector Crouch takes the saddle this time & this 3-3 progressive 4yo could have more to offer.
Looked good in the latter stages of the Lingfield trial and should come on for that. Has an inside draw which will give him an edge.

POPMASTER looks ready to win again. He went up to a rating of 109 around this time last year but arrives here on a mark of only 99, which is 1lb lower than his last winning mark. He's gone close in a few races since his last win but without getting his head in front.
Comes over from Ireland and has the advantage from the wide draw of being an early speed horse. Has every chance if getting on or near the lead.

Fantastic Fox didn’t get the rub of the green at Doncaster but had been in solid form beforehand and is generally a reliable type. Back over a C&D that suits, and with a trainer-jockey combo that does well in AW handicaps (223 runs, 57 wins, 1.04 A/E, +21pts @ 9% ROI), he’s got every chance of bouncing back and being right on the premises.

Cracking Gold took a good step forward when winning after wind surgery when last out. Although up 5 lbs for that, it still puts him well-weighted to be involved in today's C2 as I always expect more when second up after wind surgery EW 4P.

Apiarist was solid when winning at Southwell off 93 but found things tougher in the Lincoln off 98. This is a much easier task and he’s got a good record on tapeta, though the handicapper might still have him. Has a chance if things fall right.

Has winning form here, and a stiff 6f looks ideal as long as there is pace. Put a line through LTO when held up and getting no luck in running. A massive eye-catcher. Different jockey this time and must be a huge player.

Heathcliff needs to be taken on here given J Fanshawe’s 14% SR (A/E 0.43) with favourites in April on the AW (0/8 when C1-3) and D Egan’s 11% SR (A/E 0.28) on favourites carrying up to 8-11. Fivethousandtoone has to overcome T Easterby’s 7% SR (A/E 0.32) with fancied runners in C1-3 races, meanwhile the C Cox yard are yet to get rolling this spring (1/15, A/E 0.31) which puts me off Diligent Harry. I can pick holes in the remainder but old friend MARSHMAN should be incredibly competitive now back in handicap company after failing to get a clear run in the Cammidge Trophy at Doncaster last month. The son of Harry Angel had been thriving on the AW this winter, notching up a C2 handicap win over C&D, a listed success at Lingfield and 1/2l 2nd in the same sphere at Southwell. HA’S 38% SR (A/E 2.0) with runners trained in Middleham provides further cause for optimism and 6/1 looks value.

Fivethousandtoone has not won recently but did win this last year. He changed yards this year and has not been far away for all three runs, including a fourth in listed company. I think the return here, just 3 lbs heavier than that last win and having Oisin Murphy back in the saddle, could be worth a chance.

Saint Lawrence won at Listed level and was placed in a Group 3 as a two-year-old. He has only won once since, but off his lowest ever handicap mark, was only beaten 3.75 lengths in a similar race over course and distance in January. He looks a good each way bet with 4 places on offer.

This lad has only run in 3 handicaps in his career and been placed in all three. The circumstances of the race suit him. The jockey and trainer have a strike rate of over 20%. He is drawn on the better side of the straight, has won 2 of his 3 races here, and as this may be falsely run, Rossa can get him rolling quickly when needed from there. Not interested if shorter than 7s.

Another solid performer at the trip and in the grade. Got his nose in front last time after a few good runs that he didn't see out. Potentially quite well handicapped if building on that victory. Yard in decent enough form and do well in classy sprint handicaps and at the track.

Not too many miles on the clock for the 6yo. Two runs this year, not beaten far three weeks ago in a decent contest and could be ready to strike. He does tend to keep his form once fit and in good shape. He was a close 3rd over this 6f C/D last summer in a Group 3 - didn’t have a clear run, and was beaten by two runners rated 114+. His mark of 105 for this handicap gives him every chance.

A 10 times career winner and useful sprinter rated as high as 104 last year. Has been in good form this year with a good win at Southwell back in January followed by a creditable second here the month after. Looked unlucky last time out over this trip at Southwell when badly hampered and could not get a clear run and must have a solid chance here off bottom weight.

We can hang our hats on a decent-looking run from COACHELLO in a class two over this trip in January from higher in the handicap. Offish runs on polytrack and turf since then, but should feel more at home on tapeta. Very competitive renewal, so don't go crazy, but there's a definite chance of a place.

Returned back to good form LTO when a useful 2 of 10 here last February. I don't see an issue going up in class considering he's a 3-time C&D winner, but going up in class and career high mark is the bigger challenge.

There looks to be a real lack of pace here with only two prominent racers who are separated by almost the full width of the track - We Never Stop (stall 2) and Golden Mind (stall 15). 6f at Newcastle tends to favour those ridden prominently, whilst high draws also come out best. So preference is for Golden Mind, who drops back to 6f having found 7f stretching the last twice. His record at this trip is 1-5-1, with the 5th coming in a Listed contest over C&D last autumn, and he's still unexposed at sprinting trips having been campaigned over further. Blinkers go on today, suggesting they aren't going to hang around, and a mark of 99 is just 1lb higher than when winning over this trip three starts back. Every chance he can blast his rivals away from the front.
Eddie Greatrex gets this one ride today for Jack Channon, who thankfully sticks by him. Cajetan certainly looks a good bet to nothing on this AW racing day after a couple of excuses in its last runs.

Old Harrovian looked a class above when overcoming trouble to win well off 89 here last time and still looks well treated based on his novice form. Top jockey’s back on board, the yard’s in form, and with course form in the book (107 runs, 23 wins, 1.36 A/E, +33pts @ 30% ROI), he’s got a big shout of following up.

Won 2 races at Southwell in eye-catching style and hasn't finished improving yet for trainer Roger Varian. Needs to step up to his new handicap mark of 97, but the way he finished off his race last time suggests that it's possible.
Solid performer in this grade of race and at this distance. Good draw, yard in top form, go well here and useful claimer on board to take 5lbs off.

Smart Hero has only had two runs this year and won both of them, with the second win being by a bigger margin after taking on weight and stepping up in class. He still seems well-weighted for this step again to C2.

POWER OF DESTINY should find ten furlongs suitable as a fresh filly and she represents high-profile owners and trainer. She should still be improving as a four year old filly and given time since last seen she is already an all-weather winner likely just as effective on Tapeta.

Salamanca wasn’t given the easiest task at Chelmsford last time but ran on well for fourth and should strip fitter for that. First try on Tapeta, but with a strong jockey booking and a yard that does well in AW handicaps at Newcastle (29 runs, 6 wins, 1.73 A/E, +16pts @ 54% ROI), she’s one to keep on side if things fall right.

Third in this race last year from the same mark. Is a 9-year-old now, so is giving up plenty to younger legs, but he has been plotted back via an identical route as he took last year and might just outrun his price.

Has the highest mark in this field and also a C&D winner. I think he found the switch back to turf a bit tricky LTO at Doncaster, so hoping he welcomes the return back to AW. Dropping down in class should help.

CLAYMORE is touch and go due to the hit and miss form of late, but the handicap mark keeps dropping and there's potential for him to bounce back at a big price. Hollie Doyle is a plus in the saddle and she could get this one in the frame from this reduced weight. Another very competitive handicap but not without claims.
Has been in good form and finished a good 3rd of 9 over this course and distance last time out. Holds an each-way chance again.

C&D champion. Since his last win in 2023, he has participated in 18 races. He secured a 3rd place, finishing just over 3 lengths behind Glen Buck in a handicap at Southwell 55 days ago, demonstrating a strong late charge after being pushed back in the field. This 6-year-old is consistently dependable, and with Kieran O'Neill aboard, who boasts 20 wins and 56 placements here, looks even more reliable. The each-way price at 50/1 looks fantastic value.

Veteran, who showed plenty of ability, still remains when going close in a good race at Wolverhampton on Boxing Day. Well beaten only start since at Kempton last month, but should take a step forward from that. So, it would be no surprise to see him run well at a price this afternoon.

Gelded son of Le Havre who showed promise in novices and absolutely bolted up over 12 furlongs in February. Solid effort in defeat at Wolverhampton last time and still retains plenty of potential so should take all the beating this afternoon.

ROARING LEGEND has been fruitful to follow this season and I see no reason to abandon him today at 3/1. Plage De Havre has come in for support but the step up to 16.5f is a question mark especially given A Balding’s 11% SR (A/E 0.35) with fancied runners over the trip, meanwhile M Bell holds a poor record at Newcastle (14% SR, A/E 0.48 when fancied) which makes Duke Of Oxford easy to oppose. Wonder Legend is the biggest danger in my eyes but he’s running off his highest-ever mark and has only raced once over 2 miles, coming off a 4lb lower mark. I can’t make a case for the double-digit runners so it just makes sense to stick with the jolly who’s yet to lose for the H Palmer yard (3/3). The son of Roaring Lion couldn’t have won those contests much easier and has clearly taken the step up to this level in his stride; he’s got top weight to burden for that but I’m not sure we’ve seen his ceiling yet. He’s got a positive draw, top + blue FlatStats rating plus Palmer’s 62% SR (A/E 1.75) with 5yo favs in handicaps to boost claims.

Some consistent winning stayers line up in a competitive handicap. Wonder Legend is lightly raced and the last 5 runs have figures - 23121. He likes all the artificial surfaces and last time dominated here over 1m 5f and was clear and untroubled passing the line, so this 2 miles should suit him more than the opposition.

Gelded son of Derby winning Masar. Definitely gets the trip. Won at 2miles in a class 3 at Southwell and then 2nd place in a Class 4 at Southwell. Bottom weight, couple of lbs out of the handicap but notable jockey booking. Yard are in good form and go well in these sort of races.

Six horses have won LTO in this field, and fortunately, Midnight Lion is one of them. It was at this course last month, but going up in trip and going up two classes makes life harder. However, current form gives him a chance.
Tortured Soul has won 8 of his 27 starts, with two coming here at Lingfield. His last win was in January, and he has been runner-up in his 3 starts since. He looks sure to go well again here.

Destinado bounced back from a couple of bum runs when winning the apprentice race at Doncaster - winning by nearly 2 lengths with Mason Paetel, who retains the ride. He won on Thursday aboard Overnight Oats at Ripon, which was a peach of a ride. James Owen has picked up no less than 9 winners from the last 24 runners, which is a huge plus. Speed figures suggest anything close to the last run at Doncaster will go a long way to winning this. 2 wins from the last 3 visits to Lingfield is another tick in the box. Has also won off a 7lb higher rating in the past, so a 5lb penalty for the last win may not be enough to stop Destinado. NAP
They are dropping this one down in grade, and they have got a 3 lbs claiming jockey booking/change as this is his only ride of the day. A good value each way bet for the 5 places available.

Blew the start ( not a normal trait) in a class 3 handicap over extended 1.1 miles @ Wolverhampton LTO and no chance afterwards. Better back in this class 4 off 2lb lower mark, is a dual C/D winner so goes well here @ Lingfield, fast run race will suit, good pilot who retains ride allowed 5lb in this apprentice race and very shrewd trainer is in very good form @ present, making current 20/1 decent Ew value in the race.

A very open middle-distance handicap where Raintown looks great value at 14/1. He won well here a couple of runs back and should be competitive from 3 pounds higher. He likes to race on the front end and may get the run of the race.
Winner at Southwell in January. Decent efforts in defeat since and has dropped back down to that last winning mark so should run well this afternoon.
Mr Baloo boasts an excellent record on similar going, winning 4 from 6. Proven on this surface and consistently placing in class, he's a lively contender here.

Cephalus won on this day last year, following up his C&D win 7 days earlier by beating Dingle over 8f under a 5lbs penalty from a mark of 81. Blinkers went back on two starts back with instant results, finishing 2nd at Chelmsford at this 10f trip before winning back down at 8f LTO. Raised 5lbs for that, he's up to a mark of 83, which is just 2lbs higher than last year. With the stable in good form, he can win again on AW finals day.

Just the 4th start for the Williams team and has been improving each time. Last time out was a close 4th at Wolves, shaping like this trip will bring further improvement. The mark of 84 looks very workable, especially based on the 5 lengths behind Volterra in a handicap last year. 5 lbs lower now.

Struggled after picking up two wins in first four starts for Julie Camacho but signs of a revival when 3rd on second start since wind surgery at Newcastle last month. Needs to back that up but should run well if doing so.
5-time winner whose last win was twice on the all-weather at Southwell this year. Should go well over this longer trip and holds an each-way chance.
Hitched last won here back in January and is now just 1 lb above that last winning mark. It could benefit from the return to 1m2f today while up in class to C3, which is why I'm EW 4P.

Good odds for a horse that probably, on paper, is the best here. After a recent break and wind operation with a 7lb claimer on board who won on penultimate start, I think it can go well for a yard in form. Has form ahead of Kings Code, which is solid benchmark form and could be a better model now.

This son of Lope De Vega takes part in what looks like an open race. He's been frustrating recently but the drop back to a mile with an extra 1lb relief from the handicapper may give Dragon Icon his first win in some time. SDS has been booked and takes over from regular jockey Jack Mitchell.
Blue Prince is now on his last winning mark and is a reliable sort who deserves to win again. He was 2nd just 9 days ago and was only beaten by a nose. He's the one to beat here.

Dingle looked sharp when winning at Kempton off 77 and the form has been well boosted since. While Lingfield’s tighter track might not play perfectly to his strengths, he’s clearly in top form and still looks a major player if he gets the right setup.

Hasn't won since reeling off a quick hat-trick in the autumn but has been running well in defeat and was a solid 4th in a class 2 over course and distance last time. Should be bang there back down in class 3 this afternoon.
Has been in good form and has won on both of the last 2 starts. This is more difficult, but in current form, has every chance in a hat-trick attempt.

Dembe looked to have a bit up his sleeve when scoring comfortably at Newcastle and is thriving with four wins from his last six. He’s gone up again and hasn’t won off a mark this high yet, but the yard’s in great form and do well in all weather handicaps (271 runs, 42 wins, 1.09 A/E, +85pts @ 31% ROI).

Legal Reform has been on a roll since winning at the start of the year with three wins and two places out of five runs. Last month, it took the step up to C3 and was a very close second. It's worth another shot.

Going in the right direction for sure, especially with a credible 2 of 12 at Wolverhampton last month and also finishing 8 of 22 at Doncaster LTO last month. Helped by dropping down in class, so has a chance.

Silky Wilkie hasn’t been at his best on the AW lately but was third in the Ayr Gold Cup off a much higher mark in the autumn, so he’s seriously well treated if rediscovering that turf form. Big player if anywhere near that level today.

Westmorian was impressive at Southwell over this trip and looked to have more in hand than the margin suggests. The form’s taken a few hits, but he’s unexposed, open to improvement, and could go well again if handling Polytrack on his first try.
Diamondonthehill has been improving, including a C4 second here last time out, and could improve for this step up to C2 with the top draw. Gets Billy to help out as well EW 4P.
Pals Battalion is a consistent performer with strong form at this distance and on similar going, thrives in a visor and looks primed for another big run.
Party Bear is improving in leaps and bounds and has the ability to take this and run up a hat-trick of wins. Karl Burke's yard has him primed.

5th of 11 in a Class 2 over course and distance on penultimate start off a 2-pound higher mark, beaten 4.25 lengths. Has the additional benefit of the 3-pound allowance claimed in the saddle by Jack Doughty today and eased in grade to Class 4.
Only win from 10 starts was at this track over 5f. Has some solid form over 6f and is likely to appreciate this longer distance. Holds an each-way chance.

Strictly on form, it looks to have little chance, but they have traveled a long way for this race, and he gets a lot of weight from the older horses. The jockey takes off 5 lbs and has a reasonable mid-field draw. This is a good stable that knows how to place their horses, and the step-up to 7f should see improvement from this lightly raced individual.

RED FLYER is a proven stayer who is well handicapped 6lb below his last winning mark. He also has proven form in deeper races than he faces today and he has the considerable assistance of Luke Morris in the saddle. Freshened up potentially set aside for this specific race he makes plenty of each-way appeal.

Those ridden forward will be favoured and this mare will be handy enough and appreciating the step back up in trip. Kingscote is backable around here and the trainer has a strong enough record. At bottom weight she is in with every chance and backable at 8s.

Dual-purpose type who flits between hurdling and staying flat races. Is a previous CD winner here in December 2024 in class 5, winning off a mark of 70. Is running off 71 today, the same mark as when running here 17 days ago, finishing 3rd, narrowly beaten by one of today's rivals, Dance Time, but who is now better off at weights. Although that race was over 13f, today's step up to 16f should suit more.
Has been in good form this year, winning 4 consecutive races before finishing 3rd last time. Should go well again and holds an each-way chance.

THE CRAFTYMASTER blows hot and cold but looks well handicapped if getting back to his usual consistent self here. Found a Class 2 here a touch too hot in February but has two wins and a second over this trip in the back catalogue, with the second recorded from only a pound lower in the handicap. There's potential for this one to get involved from out the back.

Backspin justified support when scoring at Southwell and looked to have more in the tank, even if the form hasn’t worked out strongly. He’ll be better with a strong pace to aim at and with a trainer-jockey combo that does well in AW handicaps (261 runs, 61 wins, 1.20 A/E, +61pts @ 21% ROI), he’s still one to take seriously.

A small play here as this lad still has plenty of questions to answer on handicap debut, but he won a novice well last time out at Southwell with the runner-up subsequently winning. He has a nice draw for his run style, and whilst Hills hasn't had a winner here in the last year, his record in the long term here is good.

THE ACTOR was once well regarded by his former trainer and now taking in his second run following wind-surgery changing headgear he could be a player. Bundles of value on offer from the overnight market and given his new yard do well with sprinters he could surprise.

NOGO'S DREAM may find the combination of five furlongs on Chelmsford's Polytrack and Ryan Moore aboard suits. He has multiple sprint placed efforts and still looking well treated with the yard among the recent winners he could find the key to unlock the door here.

Aces Wild looks sure to go well in this Sprint Handicap. He has won 4 of his 24 starts, being placed on 8 other occasions. His last win was at Wolverhampton in July last year and he was placed in 2 of his 3 starts earlier this year. Second on his only previous start here at Chelmsford, he looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Hit The Line was full of running when winning over 6 furlongs at Wolverhampton on the first of April and is likely to be produced late here too.
Charlie Mason looked very good when winning last time out. There seemed to be more in the engine, and today's trip should be ideal. Just about at an each-way price for money back 4 places.

A good record so far in AW handicaps over today's trip, 1211. Steps up in grade today, but the manner of his last two wins suggests there's more to come. Should be fitter for that last run after absence also and is well drawn here.

Has not been getting beat that far of late and mark has tumbled from 74 to 66 here in just 5 runs. Is a C/D winner, good jockey retains ride and very shrewd trainer who excells in the sprinting game, is 15 percent with a Lsp of 62.37 on his 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 18/1 worth Ew consideration in the race.
Christmas Gift appears to be improving all the time and is 5 pounds better off than the top two in the market. Ryan Moore takes the ride and Balding is in red hot form, so this gets the NAP.
Unlucky in running when runner-up at Newcastle last time out. Returning to seven furlongs should help his cause along with the booking of a really strong rider.
Thomas Aquinas hadn't shown much before finishing second last time out behind a decent horse. There's enough to suggest that with a nice weight here, he can go close.

Forever Proud has been falling down the handicap and is now a pound below her last winning mark from Kempton in January. James Owen now tries blinkers on her for the first time after she disappointed as a beaten favourite, finishing only 5th of 8 at Wolverhampton 13 days ago.

Has been knocking on the door in similar handicaps. Strong finishing type who benefits from fast early pace setups. Tom Marquand rides with confidence, and connections look to have found a winnable opportunity. Form holds up well and the horse’s consistency makes him a reliable each-way or win bet.

Yet to win for Ian Williams and only 2-27 overall but has run well a couple of times this winter when 2nd at Southwell and Wolverhampton. Lurking on career low mark and well worth this first try at 7 furlongs so would be no surprise to see him run well.

Charlatan was hampered last time out, and that ninth placing would best be forgiven when assessing chances of this, I feel. 16-3-7 record in this ground. Placed on the course. Callum Shepherd clicks with the horse well, as his 9-4-2 record attests. That third at Wolverhampton at penultimate run was solid. Has ability as demonstrated by winning three in a row last term and then winning first-up in current preparation. It all adds up to a better effort this time of asking.

CAPUCHINERO is dropping in the weights and it would be a timely bounce back to form if she can match the run she showed here last Halloween when just missing out, in this grade, from seven pounds higher in the weights. Has a course win to her name and the draw looks favourable. With not much front-running around here in the stalls, she could get a handy position and be difficult to shift.

ENPASSANT has ran well over C&D off higher marks in the past. The 4 year old gelding has dropped back down to his last winning mark and also drops from a Class 4 (0-78) race to a Class 6 (0-65) here. I like his draw in stall 1 and in a 16-runne race where it looks like there could be plenty of pace on this could be set up nicely for him. Anyway, he looks well-worth an each way interest for 5 places at 11/1.
Kondratiev Wave only missed out by a neck last time out and goes again with the same mark but gets Tom Marquand to help out this time. I expect more.

This 8-year-old has won 4 times on this course, with his last triumph in April. Recently, he placed 10th out of 11 in a handicap at Lingfield 8 days ago. We can consider that a misstep, and if he shows up in good form, finishing in the top spots should be straightforward, and an each-way wager at 18/1 could be quite profitable.
Lord Danielson looked on a road to improvement last time out and has so much weight in hand here off the market leader. A few others can definitely hit the front 5.

Dark Dreamer has been struggling for form and was well beaten again last time, but the step up in trip might help, and he’s now dangerously well handicapped if he can bounce back. The yard is in form and has a good record in handicaps at Chelmsford (195 runs, 22 wins, +84pts @ 43% ROI), so it's not impossible he sparks back to life.

This consistent performer thrives over this trip and has shown marked improvement this season. Jockey James Owen knows the horse well. Conditions suit perfectly and race pace maps ideally for a stalk-and-pounce ride. Weight is fair and draw is favorable. Should go very close if repeating recent efforts.

SIXPACK runs for a shrewd dual-purpose yard and this middle-distance racer was a winner for his former trainer in Ireland. Plenty of all-weather winning form in his family , so with Tom Marquand booked the chances are this one will be ready today.

Don Simon ran well on his first run for six months at Newcastle in March when giving Turquino a race, beaten half a length in 2nd over twelve and a half furlongs. He now tries fourteen furlongs for the first time.

This 10-year-old has proven to be inconsistent, with 24 races since his last victory in 2022. Recently, he finished 5th of 6 in a handicap race at Lingfield. However, when motivated, he has shown he can perform well. Trainer Mike Murphy and his team, boasting a 20% win rate, will leverage their experience and knowledge from achieving 11 wins and 25 placements at this track to maximize the gelding's potential. At odds of 50/1, I believe an each-way bet could yield a profit.

Sky Majesty won all three of her two-year-old races, including at Group 3 and Group 2 last year, all on turf. There is no reason to think she will not cope with the all-weather at Chelmsford, especially with a good draw near the inside in stall 2.

Jouncy ran with credit in the Group 1 Middle Park and brings easily the best form into this. Handles Polytrack, and while he might need the run after a break, he’s the class act in the field and the one to beat if near ready. Yard going well too.

My only play at Chelmsford this afternoon comes in the form of ANDESITE at 12/1 each way. I understand why Sky Majesty is market leader, however Blue Point tend to hate Chelmsford (6% SR, A/E 0.31) and W Haggas’s 16% SR (A/E 0.49) over 6f here adds even less confidence. Juddmonte do pretty poorly with their geldings on the AW (15% SR, A/E 0.37 when fancied) which makes Jouncy short enough, meanwhile Sayidah Dariyan carries a poor FlatStats rating alongside W Buick’s poor 7% SR (A/E 0.46) on moderately-fancied runners on the AW. The rest all carry red FS ratings too, so are unlikely to offer much value, but Andesite was a debut winner in a C2 novice event at York last may and was thrown into Gr2 NTO and probably couldn’t cope with the heat. The son of Pinatubo may not take to the Polytrack but he looks worth a chance at this level, especially given Clipper Logisitic’s impressive 41% SR (A/E 1.71) with 3yo’s over 6f.

Star Pupil looked better than ever when winning comfortably at Wolverhampton last time and has no issues with conditions here. The yard’s flying and does well in handicaps at Chelmsford (243 runs, 50 wins, 1.13 A/E, +57pts @ 24% RO), so he’s got a strong chance of going in again if holding that form.

CHARMING WHISPER would have finished much closer with a clear run through latest. He is third-up for this spell and is a four year old still open to progress not entirely exposed for all-weather racing. Plenty of potential for this runner to perform above market expectation.

Gunlock started off with a couple of good runs for Karl Burke, finishing runner-up on debut. Then he won his maiden on the second start, both over a mile at Newcastle. He failed to progress for Burke and was subsequently sold on. The latest two runs for the new handler have been better efforts. The latest came over this course and distance when poorly drawn. He has a much better draw today.
Three-time winner whose last win came in September 2023 but has dropped in weight to 1 lb below that last winning mark. Holds an each-way chance if finding best form.

Caspian King was 5th when last seen 212 days ago. That race has worked out really well, with 6 of the runners winning since then, including a Listed race. One of them has won 3 times. He is wearing a tongue tie for the first time, and if fit, he has to go close.
Won last time out at Kempton by a nose in March. Notimeforchitchat has a 50% strike rate on the all-weather.

GOLDEN GARDEN is a sole entry across the all-weather meetings today and this three year old looks worth a tilt at this ten furlong trip. He takes on his own age group now handicapping and with his American sire he should ultimately find his way in this sphere of racing.

Scarlet Sunset completed a double at Wolverhampton over 8.5f, then 9.5f, before being hemmed in over 12f at Southwell last time, finishing 5th out of 7, just over 2 lengths behind. Worth another look back at 10f.

Anthropologist showed plenty of initial promise last year but was inconsistent when going handicapping. Finally broke his maiden tag on the penultimate run of last season. Failed to back that up on the subsequent run and was given a break and gelded over the winter. Could be the type to do well this year as his pedigree suggests he should be an improver from 2 to 3.

The 3yo has 1 win from 5. He was 3rd in a good quality AW handicap two weeks ago, after coming off a 7 month break, something to build on and the benefit of that recent run will be a positive factor. His novice stakes win on his third start last year is decent looking form. He looks overpriced.

The 4yo was progressive last year, winning his final three starts during the autumn. No problem with the winter break and was a good 3rd last week over this 7f C/D, in a good quality handicap - always having a bit too much to do after a slow start but stayed on well. Same mark for this contest and he should be better for that last run.

The 4yo was quite busy last year, 3 wins and useful on his day. No ill effect earlier in the month after returning from a 6 month break, 3rd of 10 in a good quality handicap, only outpaced in the last 100 yards. Something to build on and is on a handy looking mark.

Not too many miles on the clock for the 4yo. Progressive last year, winning three in a row last summer, including a useful £52K handicap over this 14f trip - only 3lb higher now. A big run earlier in the month after coming off his winter break, beaten under a length in a good quality Listed race. Back in handicap company for this contest and every chance he can continue the improvement this year.

The 5yo has been below par this winter but got his act together five weeks ago, never in trouble when winning a four runner contest by 7L. His stats suggest he should be better on this quicker ground - he won a decent £16K handicap last autumn on quick ground. Still on a decent mark and his six rivals don’t look great.

The ground is riding pretty quick at Haydock as I write this, but they are forecast 14 hours of rain, albeit not heavy, from Friday evening until Saturday lunchtime. So what effect that will have on watered ground is moot. In going for Tom Lacey's 9yo, I'm sure he'll be fine on either good or good to soft going, and he appears to be on a winning mark.

Just four hurdle runs for the unexposed 6yo, form 2313. He ran a good race on his handicap debut five weeks ago - over this 3m trip - he was in second and poised to challenge 2 out but made a mess of the hurdle, losing his momentum, not given a hard time after and stayed on nicely to finish third. Something to build on. Same mark for this handicap, strong jockey booking and too early to write off.

The 11yo took well to fences in the last 12 months, winning three times. His last race was maybe one run too many. Two starts back he was beaten just 2L by the smart ‘Numitor’, who has boosted that form since and the selection now meets that rival on 10lb better terms in this race. He loves the quicker ground and has been kept under wraps for the last 5 months with this nice £51K veterans’ chase prize being the target.
